study type: Network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials and observational studies
exposure: Intubation and surfactant administration followed by immediate extubation (InSurE)
cohort: The study included 13,234 preterm neonates with respiratory distress syndrome.
finding: Compared with InSurE, surfactant administration via thin catheters was associated with significantly lower rates of mortality, mechanical ventilation, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, periventricular leukomalacia, and necrotising enterocolitis.
